properties.name: The second cause, found only because the skill was run late: the reachability instrument is wired into no gate at all, so fixing its filter would leave an instrument nobody runs
properties.statement:
FOUND 2026-09-07 BY RUNNING THE ROOT-CAUSE SKILL AFTER THE CAUSE HAD ALREADY BEEN WRITTEN, which is the wrong order and is why this is a separate record rather than a line in the first one. Anthony asked whether the skill had been run on the appended field feedback or whether the class had simply been recognised from memory. It had been recognised: tier 1 was done (the design was searched on the raw terms, the class was found, the prior instances were read), and then a cause was written without step 3 - GENERATE CANDIDATES FROM THE DESIGN - ever happening. The skill's own warning describes the failure exactly: the first plausible explanation arrives, it feels like understanding, and it gets written down.

STEP 3, RUN PROPERLY, PRODUCED FOUR CANDIDATES INSTEAD OF ONE:
(a) The instrument's filter fuses reachability with adoption, so a schema default hides an unreachable property. This was the recorded cause.
(b) Nothing OBLIGES a typed constructor to cover its own type's declared properties; the constructors are hand-picked subsets and no rule says otherwise.
(c) The observation is wrong - some tool does accept priority under another name.
(d) The instrument is never RUN, so its filter is irrelevant to whether anything gets caught.

THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, taken 2026-09-07: grep for vocabulary_reach across .github/workflows/, every tools/*.py and the Makefile returns NOTHING outside the script itself. The CI job runs 20+ gates - validate_schema, skill_lint, check_doc_versions, reflow2_check, check_intent_authority, check_command_surface and more - and vocabulary_reach is not among them. It is a manual instrument that runs when somebody remembers it. Candidate (c) is refuted by the same sweep: the string priority appears in no toolsnap, so no tool accepts it under any name.

SO (a) AND (d) ARE BOTH TRUE AND THEY ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. The filter explains why the instrument would not have reported these two properties even if somebody had run it. The wiring explains why nobody ran it. Fixing only the filter yields a correct instrument that still reports to nobody, which by the skill's step 6 means the CLASS stays open and only this instance closes.

WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT THE FIX, which is why it was worth finding: the v0.52.0 item is not one change but two - unfuse the filter so reachability is asked without a usage precondition, AND run the pass in CI so the answer reaches somebody. The second is the cheaper half and the one that makes the first matter.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the instrument SHOULD be a blocking gate or a reported note. That is the same enforced-versus-advisory question Anthony ruled on for the four rules today, and it has not been put to him for this. Nor was it established why the instrument was left unwired - no decision in the record says it was deliberate, and absence of a decision is not evidence of an oversight.
